lead: Tongue posture for voice is the idea, circulated in looksmaxxing and voice-training circles, that resting the tongue against the roof of the mouth, as in mewing, improves vocal resonance and gives a fuller, deeper-sounding voice. It extends mewing, which people practise for jawline and facial structure, to how they sound.[1]

Mewing is named after British orthodontist John Mew, who developed the practice of orthotropics with his son Mike Mew; proponents say pressing the tongue against the palate can reshape the jaws and improve facial structure.[1] Wikipedia reports that the American Association of Orthodontists states there is no evidence mewing improves the jaw, and that interest surged from January 2019 through social media and looksmaxxing communities.[1] The article does not discuss claims about the voice.[1]

Voice science does recognise a link between tongue position and sound: the mouth, throat and nasal cavities filter the buzzing source from the vocal folds, and tongue height and frontness set the first two formants, which mostly determine vowel quality.[2] No study was found testing sustained resting tongue posture as a way to change a person's voice.

chain: Tongue held at the palate at rest
Claimed change in oral and facial structure and space
Claimed shift in resonance and voice tone
angle.text: Practitioners hold the tongue against the palate with the aim of improving facial structure and, by extension, how resonant their voice sounds. The voice effect is a claim made by practitioners.

paras: Practitioners rest the whole tongue against the palate as a habit. The mewing claim is that sustained tongue pressure reshapes the jaws and face.[1] The voice version holds that the resulting oral space and structure alter resonance.

The vocal folds produce a rich buzzing source and the vocal tract filters it. The peaks that result, called formants, come from resonances of the tract.[2] Tongue position and mouth shape set the first two formants: F1 rises for open, low vowels and falls for high ones, and F2 rises for front vowels and falls for back ones.[2] Lip rounding lowers the formants, and vocal tract length scales the resonances overall.[2] Voice coaches use these relationships when training resonance.

Wikipedia reports that no credible research has proven orthotropics effective, that most orthodontists do not regard mewing as an alternative to jaw surgery, and that Mike Mew was struck from the UK dental register in 2024 following a misconduct hearing.[1] Interest spread especially through looksmaxxing subcultures after 2019.[1]

timeline.event: Interest in mewing surges on social media.[1]
Mike Mew struck from the UK dental register.[1]

name: Tongue posture for voice

card.summary: Applying mewing to the voice; the base practice is unproven and no voice study exists.
card.note: Extension of a claim that professional bodies say lacks evidence.

quick.overview:
This is the claim that resting the tongue on the palate, as in mewing, shifts voice resonance. It is a minor offshoot of the mewing trend.

No studies have tested it, and orthodontic bodies say there is no evidence mewing changes the jaw.
quick.mechanism: Practitioners hold the tongue against the roof of the mouth, and proponents propose that resulting changes in oral structure alter resonance.
quick.risks: The posture itself is not reported as harmful in the sources reviewed, but the broader mewing practice is described as unproven, and its main proponent faced a misconduct finding over child patients.
